problemStatement.formal:
Is there a covering system all of whose moduli are of the form $p-1$ for some primes $p\geq 5$?



Selfridge has found an example using divisors of $360$ if $p=3$ is allowed.

The key constraint: excluding p=3 removes modulus 2, so all moduli ≥ 4 — very restrictive for covering

All p-1 moduli for p≥5 are even because p≥5 implies p is odd

The obstruction is quantitative: need sum ≥ 1 but easy primes only give 0.606
Product ∏m_i is simpler than LCM for positivity proofs (Finset.prod_pos vs no Finset.lcm_pos)
Int.ofNat_toNat gives ↑n.toNat = max n 0 (not = n); need max_eq_left for nonneg case
